GeoQC Flow

Sharper Shape GroupGeospatial Data EngineerInternal production tooling

Source code is not public. GeoQC Flow is internal tooling built for Sharper Shape production use, so the repository stays private. The implementation details below are described rather than linked for that reason. Happy to walk through the architecture in conversation.

A Python CLI tool that automates quality control across multi-step FileGDB pipelines — comparing layers step by step, classifying geometry changes by severity, detecting real attribute edits versus system noise, and generating professional interactive HTML and DOCX reports from a single command.

Usage

# Activate environment and run
conda activate geoqcflow
geo-qc-flow run --pipeline-folder "C:\path\to\pipeline" --output "C:\path\to\reports"

Key capabilities

Auto-discovery

Detects numbered step folders and FileGDB files automatically. No hardcoded filenames — just point it at a pipeline folder and run.

Smart feature matching

Auto-detects unique ID fields (≥90% uniqueness). Falls back to index-based matching for layers without structured IDs.

Real change detection

Distinguishes genuine edits from system noise — whitespace normalisation, null handling, and case differences are filtered out before flagging.

Smart remarks engine

Rule-based system auto-generates colour-coded alerts, warnings, and info notices flagging high-change layers, identical steps, and derived layers.

Geometry severity classification

Every layer comparison is assigned a geometry severity band based on the percentage of features with real spatial displacement:

None — 0% Stable — <2% Light — 2–10% Moderate — 10–25% Major — >25%

Context

Developed during my work at Sharper Shape to address a real gap in our GIS pipeline QA process. Geospatial datasets pass through multiple processing steps — digitisation, QA review, independent check, final delivery — and tracking what actually changed between steps was previously a manual, time-consuming task.

GeoQC Flow automates that process entirely. It handles heterogeneous layer structures, variable ID field naming conventions, and mixed geometry types (points, lines, polygons) within the same pipeline run. The HTML output replicates Sharper Shape's internal design system, making reports immediately familiar to the team.
